prerequisites: Knowledge of the system of units and fundamental magnitudes: Force, flow, pressure, power, etc.
Very elementary concepts of fluids (gases-air and liquids) such as: pressure, flow, force, etc. and their basic laws
Very elementary concepts of electrical circuits (V, I, R, series, parallel, etc).
Basic PC skills (word processor, spreadsheet, file manipulation, etc.)

learning_outcomes.text: The generation of pressurized fluids (air and/or oil) in the appropriate conditions for their use in the most common actuators (cylinders and motors).
The design of pneumatic and oleohydraulic circuits and their control and improvement system using various technologies.
The components of pneumatic and/or oleohydraulic circuits.
Apply the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines in engineering practice.
Evaluate the needs and possibilities that pneumatics and oleohydraulics offer for the design and optimization of specific systems and processes.
Acquire and apply the necessary knowledge and skills to understand and design pneumatic and oleohydraulic circuits with wide application in current industrial processes.
Enable the development of students' autonomous learning capacity and foster attitudes of collaboration with others and personal initiative.
Ability to solve problems: Ability to identify, analyze, and define the significant elements that constitute a problem to solve it rigorously.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

Ability to write, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing and automation processes.

syllabus_topics: Block I: Fundamentals of the operation of pneumatic and oleohydraulic systems
Topic 1. Introduction to pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
Topic 2. Preliminary concepts of Fluid Mechanics.
Topic 3. Laminar regime in pneumatic and oleohydraulic systems.
Topic 4. Turbulent regime in pneumatic and oleohydraulic systems.
Topic 5. Calculation of pressure losses in installations and systems.
Block II: Characteristic components of pneumatic and oleohydraulic installations.
Topic 6. Generation of movement in oleohydraulic systems: Pumps.
Topic 7. Generation of compressed air in pneumatic systems.
Topic 8. Pneumatic and hydraulic actuators.
Topic 9. Pneumatic and hydraulic control elements.
Topic 10. Hydraulic and pneumatic motors.
Block III: Design, test and application of pneumatic and oleohydraulic systems.
Topic 11. Simulation programs in pneumatics and oleohydraulics.
Topic 12. Applications of pneumatic and oleohydraulic systems in engineering.
Problems of control volumes applied to pneumatic and hydraulic elements.
Resolution and design in MATLAB of pneumatic/oleohydraulic systems.
Operation and design of pneumatic/oleohydraulic circuit.
Practices in the Pneumatics and Oleohydraulics Laboratory.
Final work or practice on the design of an industrial application.
teaching_methods: Demonstration of the analytical procedure to follow to build a model of a pneumatic/oleohydraulic installation within the PID 24-25 Virtual Hydropneumatics Lab
Explaining videos of various pneumatic and hydraulic components (different types of actuators, different types of pumps, etc.)
Detailed explanatory guides for the activities to be carried out
Digitization according to the Virtual Hydro-pneumatics Lab Teaching Innovation Project
Flipped classroom methodology: Virtualized theoretical content with explanations/video-explanations
Design and simulation of an oleohydraulic/pneumatic system using a flipped-classroom format (Teaching Innovation Project)

assessment_methods.method: Virtual activities, practices and other works (5% practices with report, 5% the rest)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as: 10% from virtual activities, practices and other works (5% for practices with report and 5% for the rest), 70% from the final exam, 10% from the final project, and 10% from the tutor report. To pass the subject, a minimum score of 50% of the maximum possible is required in the final exam, meaning at least 5 out of 10. There will also be a minimum score for both the theory and problem parts of the final exam. For the extraordinary call, course grades are generally maintained, but students may opt to renounce them, in which case the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade and includes additional content. Spelling mistakes in the final exam will result in a deduction from the score.
